# Lower revision revalidation — final_portability

Approve lower `5a9f044f84fbcc21597f7bf44466cab9b3694b42` for the portability/testing lens. The original F1 defect is fixed, and I could not break the new classification or its integration. Core fit: yes; deterministic Unicode classification is a small, stdlib-only repository mechanism with no runtime/provider-specific setup.

This verdict covers only the lower delta from `e126316ce6fa724b19353501a817ab89a6f08af3`. The original report and probes remain unchanged. This is not a new upper-layer verdict.

## Findings and limits

There are no remaining correctness findings in this delta. My original real-Git U+13439 probe now produces one blocking frozen-record finding for both the raw character and `𓐹`, on both Python 3.9.6 and 3.14.6. Previously both edits passed on 3.9.

The new `FORMAT_CONTROL_RANGES` contains exactly 170 of 170 `Cf` code points from the actual Python 3.14 Unicode 16.0.0 database: no missing or extra entries. I independently evaluated the production predicate for all 1,114,112 code points on each interpreter. Both classify the same 4,206 code points as protected, exactly the union of Unicode 16 `Cf` and the existing non-format ranges, with zero over/underclassification against that declared set. The classifications have identical SHA-256 `a710979a4f8f6e057f3ec3d7f3ba9dd80762c6fe96f10dee00c1256ef52fed02`.

Fourteen of fourteen additional real-Git boundary cases pass per interpreter. They cover two newly recognized controls in raw, decimal-entity, hexadecimal-entity, escaped, double-backslash, inline-code-entity, and raw-inline-code forms. Active control bytes remain frozen; visibly literal entity spellings remain editable.

AST comparison against the previous lower revision found exactly one changed shared function/class definition: `contains_default_ignorable_characters`. The older NFKC prose normalizer and all other shared parser functions/classes are unchanged. Forty of forty shared Markdown-consumer tests pass within the targeted selection below. This bounds the parser blast radius; it does not claim Unicode assignments after the explicitly pinned version are already covered. Future assignments require an explicit table update.

## Commands and actual results

All fixture-bearing commands used:

```text
PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1 TMPDIR=/private/tmp/final-portability-fixtures
```

I ran each command below once with `python3` (3.14.6) and once with `/usr/bin/python3` (3.9.6), prepending that environment and interpreter:

```text
/private/tmp/final-portability-discovery.py /private/tmp/agentfold-final-review-lower-r2 e126316ce6fa724b19353501a817ab89a6f08af3
/private/tmp/final-portability-probes.py /private/tmp/agentfold-final-review-lower-r2
/private/tmp/final-portability-lower-r2-tests.py /private/tmp/agentfold-final-review-lower-r2
/private/tmp/final-portability-controls.py /private/tmp/agentfold-final-review-lower-r2 lower
/private/tmp/final-portability-lower-r2-boundaries.py /private/tmp/agentfold-final-review-lower-r2
```

Discovery: 2 of 2 new methods discovered; AST, `unittest`, and shard selection each report 538 queue methods; 16 test files; no duplicate names or skips.

Targeted tests include both delta methods, six related Unicode/exposure tests, and the complete 40-method Markdown-consumer file:

```text
Python 3.14.6: Ran 48 tests in 9.346s — OK; failures=0 errors=0 skips=0
Python 3.9.6:  Ran 48 tests in 9.466s — OK; failures=0 errors=0 skips=0
```

Restoring the prior runtime-dependent detector in the Python 3.9 test process makes both new methods red: `Ran 2 tests in 1.570s`, `FAILED (failures=24)`, zero errors/skips. Both original mutation controls were also repeated on both interpreters: 4 of 4 control runs went red through assertions. Disabling invisible-source detection caused 12 subtest failures per interpreter; freezing all retry diagnosis caused 10 per interpreter. No control changed clone files.

The exhaustive classification commands were, in this order:

```text
PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 /private/tmp/final-portability-lower-r2-classification.py /private/tmp/agentfold-final-review-lower-r2 reference
PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 /usr/bin/python3 /private/tmp/final-portability-lower-r2-classification.py /private/tmp/agentfold-final-review-lower-r2 compare
```

The first independently derives the expected Unicode 16 set from the bundled database; the second uses that saved expected set. Both report `codepoints_checked=1114112`, `cf_codepoints=170`, `guard_codepoints=4206`, `overblocked=0`, `underblocked=0`, `skips=0`.

Logs are saved as `/private/tmp/final-portability-lower-r2-{classification,probes,tests,controls,boundaries}-{314,39}.log`; the scripts and expected set are beside them. Final `git -c core.fsmonitor=false --no-optional-locks status --porcelain=v1` is empty; `git diff --quiet --no-ext-diff` and `git diff --cached --quiet --no-ext-diff` both exit 0. HEAD remains the pinned revision.

The review used the mechanical code delta and clone contracts/code, not the delta's worklog conclusions. I did not rerun the full suite, full corpus, record-free projection, CI, or publication gates; those remain parent-owned. No clone, index, configuration, task, handover, PR, or original review artifact was changed.
